Subject: Draft success definition & QA checkpoints for 6-week evaluation

Hi Elena / Thomas —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Per our call, I’m attaching a first-pass mutual action plan focused on how MedSuite can validate latency, throughput, and extraction accuracy over a 6-week trial. Key goals here: make the evaluation low-friction, measurable, and tied to the business outcomes you mentioned (reduction in triage time, extraction F1 on clinical notes).

Highlights in the attached MAP_v1.pdf:
- Week 1: baseline ingestion + smoke tests (endpoints, auth, sample traffic)
- Weeks 2–4: steady-state load, KV/prefix caching exercises, model variants (open vs quantized)
- Week 5: edge-case concordance tests (rare diagnoses) and drift sampling
- Week 6: final pass, performance verification, runbook for cutover decision

Acceptance criteria (proposed):
- Average 95th pctl latency < 300ms on 256-token seqs under target throughput
- Inference cost per 1k tokens within 15% of the projected estimate
- Extraction accuracy: end-to-end F1 >= 0.88 on curated golden set (provided by MedSuite)
- No P0 reliability incidents during a 48-hour soak at target load

Attached is also a starter QA test catalog (qa-test-catalog.xlsx) — we’ll update with your golden set and run owners. Can you confirm: 1) the golden set delivery date, 2) whether you need a short on-site workshop for integration, and 3) any additional legal/infosec checklist items we should pre-seed into the MAP?

Next steps: once you confirm the golden set timeline we’ll lock the runbook and propose a kickoff date.

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: qa-test-catalog.xlsx (xlsx)

Quick update after running the dry-run smoke suite this morning (results attached in-line and I pushed the updated test catalog to the shared doc):

Summary: infra baseline looks sound; two configuration items to address before kickoff:
1) KV cache: bump shard memory from 8GB->12GB for the high-concurrency tests (I’ve annotated the qa-test-catalog with the sizing rationale).
2) OCR vignette: the worst-case doc lowered extraction F1 to 0.76 in an unquantized run — adding pre-processing (whitespace normalization + simple regex fixes) recovered F1 to ~0.85. We should include a small preproc step in the workshop to demonstrate mitigation.

Next steps:
- I’ve shared the updated qa-test-catalog.xlsx with Elena (link) and marked test owners.
- Marissa: can you confirm workshop time + send calendar invite with Zoom link?
